entities.summary:
Gauzelin of Toul was a French Roman Catholic prelate who served as the Bishop of Toul from 922 until his death in 962. He played a crucial role in the Carolingian Renaissance, promoting education and arts during his tenure. Gauzelin was a key figure in the Catholic Church's efforts to consolidate power and influence during the 10th century.




Gauzelin's legacy can be seen in the numerous charitable foundations and schools he established during his episcopacy, which had a lasting impact on the educational landscape of the region. His efforts to promote the arts and literature also contributed to the cultural flowering of the Carolingian period.




The exact date of Gauzelin's death is not certain, but it is believed to have occurred in September 962. He was canonized as a saint in the Catholic Church in the 17th century, recognizing his contributions to the faith and his commitment to the welfare of his people.
